newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair says vast profits made by utilities.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair says vast profits made by utilities.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Wednesday that vast excess profits were made by privatised utilities and a windfall tax on them was essential to help unemployed young people find work.

But Blair, under questioning from former prime minister John Major in the House of Commons, declined to give details of the companies which will be affected by the windfall tax, saying this was a matter for Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown.
Brown is due to announce details of the windfall tax, a key pledge in Labour's election manifesto, in the budget he is expected to unveil early in June.
"The reason for introducing the windfall tax is clear. There is no doubt at all that excess profits, vast excess profits were made, there is no doubt of that," Blair said.
"There is no doubt also that it is absolutely esesential we give hope and opportunity to those hundreds of thousands of young people presently without work in our society today."
The chairman of British Telecommunications Plc, Sir Iain Vallance, last week said the company owed it to its shareholders to legally challenge the windfall tax if it was applied to BT.
But Blair refused to be drawn by Major on whether BT would be affected.

Blair also dismissed a charge by Major that the tax would lead to higher utility prices, saying some regulators have already said it would not be right for the tax to be passed on to customers. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
